question: What is the main responsibility of the Department for Quality Assurance and Development (QSE) at the University of Bern?
groundtruth_answer: The Department for Quality Assurance and Development (QSE) ensures the coordination and implementation of the quality strategy in all areas of the university.
supporting_sentences: In collaboration with the Vice Rectorates, the staff of the University Management, and all university units, the Department for Quality Assurance and Development (Department QSE) ensures the coordination and implementation of the quality strategy in all areas of the university.

supporting_sentences: Contact

question: What is the process for institutional accreditation at the University of Bern?
groundtruth_answer: The Department for Quality Assurance and Development is responsible for the process of institutional accreditation, which was completed with a positive decision from the Swiss Accreditation Council based on a self-evaluation report and external expert review.
supporting_sentences: Furthermore, it is responsible for the process of institutional accreditation of Universität Bern, the management of the QSE Commission, as well as the networking of stakeholders in quality-related matters.
The Swiss Accreditation Council has accredited the University of Bern as a higher education institution without any conditions.

With the accreditation decision received by the University of Bern on September 24, 2021, the process of institutional accreditation could be completed (further information in the process report) (https://aaq.ch/download/universitaet-bern-unibe/)

The basis for the positive accreditation decision was a self-evaluation report prepared by the University of Bern in 2020 (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e809/e810/e812/e708931/e715528/e1059275/Selbstbeurteilungsbericht2020_ger.pdf) and the review by external experts in spring 2021.

question: How long is the University of Bern’s institutional accreditation valid?
groundtruth_answer: The accreditation is valid for a period of seven years.
supporting_sentences: The accreditation is valid for a period of seven years.

question: What is the stated purpose of course evaluation at the University of Bern?
groundtruth_answer: To provide concrete indications for the improvement of teaching/learning situations, maintain and further develop teaching quality, and serve as proof of quality to legislators and the public.
supporting_sentences: Course evaluation provides concrete indications for the improvement of teaching/learning situations and enables teaching quality at the University of Bern to be maintained at a high level and further developed. In addition, it serves as proof of quality to legislators and the public.

question: Who is responsible for selecting and registering courses for evaluation?
groundtruth_answer: The quality officers of the faculties are responsible for the selection and registration of courses and assessments to be evaluated.
supporting_sentences: The quality officers of the faculties are responsible for the selection and registration of courses and assessments to be evaluated.

question: How often should every course at the University of Bern be evaluated?
groundtruth_answer: Every course should be evaluated at least once every three years.
supporting_sentences: every course should be evaluated at least once every three years;

question: What is the minimum requirement for assessment evaluation at University of Bern?
groundtruth_answer: 50% of all assessments should be evaluated at least once every three years.
supporting_sentences: 50% of all assessments should be evaluated at least once every three years;

question: Who is required to have a final evaluation?
groundtruth_answer: For new lecturers and those in qualification positions, final evaluation is mandatory.
supporting_sentences: for new lecturers and those in qualification positions, final evaluation is mandatory.

question: What is the survey participation minimum for automatic result delivery to instructors?
groundtruth_answer: At least 5 students must participate.
supporting_sentences: To preserve student anonymity, the results of a survey are only automatically sent if at least 5 students have participated.

question: Are evaluation surveys anonymous at the University of Bern?
groundtruth_answer: Yes, all surveys are anonymous.
supporting_sentences: Yes, all surveys are anonymous. There is no way to trace who gave which answers.

question: In what languages are the course evaluation questionnaires available?
groundtruth_answer: The questionnaires for the mid-term, final evaluation, and assessment evaluation are available in German, English, and French.
supporting_sentences: The questionnaires for the mid-term, final evaluation, and assessment evaluation are available in German, English, and French (language selection using the flag symbol at the top of the survey).

question: How can students participate in a course evaluation survey?
groundtruth_answer: Instructors provide a QR code in class or a survey link by email or ILIAS for final/mid-term evaluation; for assessment evaluation, students receive a survey link by email from the Course Evaluation Office.
supporting_sentences: Final and mid-term evaluation: Instructors provide students with a QR code in class (usually on the second to last session) that leads to the survey. Alternatively, a survey link can be provided (e.g., by email or ILIAS). Assessment evaluation: Students receive a link to the survey by email from the Course Evaluation Office.

question: Why are students asked to participate in many surveys?
groundtruth_answer: Because some faculties evaluate many or all courses and assessments, students may be required to fill out a relatively high number of surveys.
supporting_sentences: The number and selection of courses and assessments to be evaluated each semester are set by the quality officers of the respective faculty. Some faculties evaluate many or all courses and assessments, so it is possible students must complete a relatively high number of surveys.

question: When is the final evaluation of a course conducted?
groundtruth_answer: Towards the end of the course sessions, from the 11th week of the semester onwards.
supporting_sentences: Standard implementation date: Towards the end of the course sessions, from the 11th week of the semester onwards.

question: How are evaluation results typically delivered to instructors?
groundtruth_answer: Instructors receive the results immediately after the survey closes via PDF report by email and can access an HTML report via a link.
supporting_sentences: Final or mid-term evaluation: instructors receive the results immediately after the survey closes. A PDF report with automatic analysis of the survey results and student comments is sent by email. In addition, an interactive HTML report can be accessed via a link in the email.

question: What is the minimum response rate required to send evaluation results?
groundtruth_answer: A minimum of 5 valid responses is required for the report to be sent.
supporting_sentences: If the response rate is sufficient (min. 5 valid responses), the report will be sent to the lecturers.

question: Should evaluation results be discussed with students?
groundtruth_answer: Yes, the framework concept stipulates that instructors should discuss the survey results, key findings, and planned improvements with students before the end of the semester.
supporting_sentences: To close the first feedback loop, the framework concept stipulates that instructors should discuss the survey results, key findings, and planned improvements with students before the end of the semester. This demonstrates to students that instructors are engaging with the feedback.

question: What happens to courses evaluated as 'excellent'?
groundtruth_answer: Courses achieving 'excellent' results are nominated for the ALL Award (Recognition of Outstanding Teaching Performance).
supporting_sentences: Final evaluations that achieve the “outstanding” level (https://www.unibe.ch/studium/werkzeuge_und_arbeitshilfen/fuer_lehrende/lehrveranstaltungsevaluation/rahmenkonzept/index_ger.html#pane1121983) are nominated for the ALL Award (Recognition of Outstanding Teaching Performance) (https://www.gutelehre.unibe.ch/foerderangebote/all/).

question: What measures are taken if a final evaluation is 'insufficient'?
groundtruth_answer: Measures for insufficient results are defined in the framework concept, and faculties may have additional measures in their own QSE guidelines.
supporting_sentences: Measures for insufficient results in a final evaluation are defined in the framework concept (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e1006/e855118/e855497/e946563/e998762/e1009019/e1009041/Rahmenkonzept_2024_Final_ger.pdf). Faculties may define additional measures in their own QSE guidelines. Minimum requirements are listed here (https://www.unibe.ch/studium/werkzeuge_und_arbeitshilfen/fuer_lehrende/lehrveranstaltungsevaluation/massnahmen/index_ger.html).

question: What are the available supplementary modules for final evaluation questionnaires?
groundtruth_answer: eLearning, Student Contributions, Team Teaching, Application Orientation, Interdisciplinarity, e-Coach Products / ILIAS Room, and Course Format.
supporting_sentences: eLearning

The “eLearning” additional module is suitable for courses that are conducted at least half in digital form (e.g., Zoom, Teams, livestream, podcast). It contains 6 questions to be answered with a 6-point scale. Additional open-text feedback can be provided.
Student Contributions

The “Student Contributions” additional module is suitable for courses in which students make substantive contributions, for example through presentations. It contains 9 questions to be answered with a 6-point scale. Additional open-text feedback can be provided.
Team Teaching

The “Team Teaching” additional module is suitable for courses taught by several instructors at the same time or alternately. It contains 7 questions to be answered with a 6-point scale. Additional open-text feedback can be provided.
Application Orientation

The “Application Orientation” additional module is suitable for courses focused on the practical application of theory. It contains 6 questions to be answered with a 6-point scale. Additional open-text feedback can be provided.
Interdisciplinarity

The “Interdisciplinarity” additional module is suitable for courses whose content spans multiple (sub-)disciplines. It contains 6 questions to be answered with a 6-point scale. Additional open-text feedback can be provided.
e-Coach Products / ILIAS Room

This additional module is only intended for instructors who participated in the e-Coach program (https://www.ecoach.unibe.ch/). It contains 4 questions about digital components and the ILIAS course room, to be answered with a 6-point scale.
Course Format

This additional module is only intended for instructors who participated in the e-Coach program (https://www.ecoach.unibe.ch/). It contains 3 questions to be answered with a 6-point scale and can be well combined with the e-Coach Products / ILIAS Room additional module.

question: What scale is used for the core final evaluation questions?
groundtruth_answer: A 6-point Likert scale is used for the questionnaire.
supporting_sentences: The questionnaire uses a 6-point Likert scale

question: What are the main criteria surveyed in the final evaluation questionnaire?
groundtruth_answer: Learning success, satisfaction with the course, level of difficulty and pace, and students’ own contribution.
supporting_sentences: The questionnaire for the final evaluation is based on the teaching quality model (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e1006/e855118/e855497/e946563/e998762/e1027399/e1027402/VRQ_Modell_Lehrqualitaet_md3_Modell_Lehrqualitaet_ger.jpg).
The following criteria are surveyed:
- Learning success (increase in knowledge and skills) (target criterion)
- Satisfaction with the course (target criterion)
- Level of difficulty and pace
- Students’ own contribution (active participation and preparation)

question: When should interim feedback be collected in a course?
groundtruth_answer: No later than by the second third of the semester, so that results can be discussed and adjustments made during the current course.
supporting_sentences: We recommend that you collect interim feedback no later than by the second third of the semester, so that the results can be discussed with students and any necessary adjustments can still be made during the current course.

question: What is the purpose of interim evaluation?
groundtruth_answer: It is purely formative, providing detailed data-based indications of areas where the course needs improvement, preparation for the final evaluation, and fostering a feedback culture.
supporting_sentences: The interim evaluation is purely formative, i.e., intended for improvement. Its purpose is to provide instructors with detailed data-based indications of areas where the course needs improvement (see Model of Teaching Quality (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e1006/e855118/e855497/e946563/e998762/e1027399/e1027402/VRQ_Modell_Lehrqualitaet_md3_Modell_Lehrqualitaet_ger.jpg)).
Furthermore, the interim evaluation can help foster an open feedback culture within a course.

question: In which languages is the interim evaluation questionnaire available?
groundtruth_answer: German, English, and French.
supporting_sentences: The questionnaire is available in German, English, and French (selectable by flag icon in the survey).

question: What are examples of formative feedback methods mentioned?
groundtruth_answer: Traffic Light Feedback, Flashlight, Target, Posters with Open Questions, Interim Tests, Muddiest Point, Peer Observation.
supporting_sentences: Survey Instruments
Traffic Light Feedback
With this survey method, you quickly (in 2–5 minutes) get an overview of the quantitative distribution of opinions, preferences, or the learning status of your students.
Flashlight
The flashlight is a qualitative survey method in which your students provide information about their learning needs, opinions, or preferences regarding your course.
Target
With the target, you can gather student feedback on various aspects of your course and their characteristics.
Posters with Open Questions
This method allows you to specifically collect qualitative feedback on the strengths and weaknesses of a course, as well as suggestions for improvement.
Interim Tests
With the data from interim tests, you can determine to what extent students have already achieved the objectives of your course.
Muddiest Point
This method is about specifically identifying and then addressing open questions that remain for students.
Peer Observation
Peer observation refers to a structured, non-evaluative exchange between instructors, where they visit each other's courses.

question: When are surveys for the evaluation of assessment performance typically conducted?
groundtruth_answer: After the assessment has taken place (usually at 8:00 p.m. on the day of the exam), from the 12th week of the semester onwards.
supporting_sentences: Standard implementation time: After the assessment has taken place (usually at 8:00 p.m. on the day of the exam), from the 12th week of the semester onwards.

question: Who can register assessments for evaluation?
groundtruth_answer: Lecturers can voluntarily register their assessments for evaluation. Usually, registration is carried out by a central office of the institute.
supporting_sentences: REGULAR

The framework concept stipulates that 50% of all assessments must be evaluated regularly (at least every 3 years). The faculties plan the evaluations accordingly and select the assessments to be evaluated, taking into account the faculty QSE guidelines.
OPTIONAL
Lecturers can voluntarily register their assessments for evaluation.

question: What aspects does the standard questionnaire for assessment evaluation cover?
groundtruth_answer: Didactic coherence, suitability of the examination format, student preparation, exam conditions, and difficulty.
supporting_sentences: CONTENT

The standardized questionnaire (https://scanserveruls.unibe.ch/evasys/online.php?p=7JDG6) for the evaluation of assessments (oral and written exams) is based on the teaching quality model (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e1006/e855118/e855497/e946563/e998762/e1027399/e1027402/VRQ_Modell_Lehrqualitaet_md3_Modell_Lehrqualitaet_ger.jpg) and covers the following dimensions:
- Didactic coherence (How well do the learning contents, the teaching methods used in the course, and the exam fit together?) (Questions 2.1-2.5)
- The suitability of the examination format (Question 3.1)
- Student preparation for the exam (Questions 4.1-4.2)
- Exam conditions (5.1-5.2)
- Difficulty of the exam (6.1).

question: How are assessments with fewer than 5 participants handled for evaluation?
groundtruth_answer: Assessment evaluations with fewer than 5 registrations will not be set up in the evaluation system.
supporting_sentences: Participant lists with at least 5 students should be available for the respective exam date. They may also be saved to KSL at a later time, but not later than one day before the exam. Assessment evaluations with fewer than 5 registrations will not be set up in the evaluation system.

question: When is the report for assessment evaluation sent to instructors?
groundtruth_answer: If the response rate is sufficient (min. 5 valid responses), the report will be sent to the lecturers, only after grades have been confirmed.
supporting_sentences: 7. Report
If the response rate is sufficient (min. 5 valid responses), the report will be sent to the lecturers. If the response rate is too low, no report will be generated.
If confirmation of grade announcement is missing, reports will only be sent to lecturers after individually agreed deadlines with the faculties (e.g., 6 weeks after the last exam).

question: How does the University of Bern define 'good teaching'?
groundtruth_answer: Teaching is considered 'good' when the intended learning outcomes, teaching and learning activities, and the assessments of learning outcomes are well aligned (didactic coherence).
supporting_sentences: Based on findings from teaching and learning research, teaching is considered "good" when three decisive factors are well aligned ("didactic coherence," English "constructive alignment"):
- the intended learning outcomes
- the teaching and learning activities
- the assessments of learning outcomes

question: What are the three main purposes of course evaluations, as outlined in the framework concept?
groundtruth_answer: Proof of quality (accountability), further development (improvement orientation), and participation rights.
supporting_sentences: Course evaluation at the University of Bern serves multiple purposes. It is carried out in the form of student surveys and thus involves students in the design of teaching (participation rights). The resulting data provides concrete indications for the improvement of teaching and learning situations (improvement orientation). Finally, it serves as a proof of quality for legislators and the public (accountability).

question: How are performance levels determined for final evaluation results?
groundtruth_answer: Based on the overall result of final evaluation (means from learning progress and satisfaction questions) with thresholds for 'excellent,' 'very good,' 'good,' 'sufficient,' and 'inadequate.'
supporting_sentences: The results of the final evaluation are assigned to one of 5 levels of success. Assignment is based on the overall result of a final evaluation. Means from questions 1.1–1.3 (learning progress) and 2.1–2.5 (satisfaction) are taken into account.
Since FS24, the following success levels and thresholds, established together with the faculties and an external expert, apply:
≥5.7 = "excellent" (dark green)
≥5.5 <5.7 = "very good" (light green)
≥4.0 <4.5 = "sufficient" (yellow)
<4.0 = "inadequate" (red)

question: Who is responsible for QSE at the course level?
groundtruth_answer: Instructors are responsible for QSE at the individual course level.
supporting_sentences: Instructors are responsible for QSE at the individual course level. They design the course taking previous evaluation results into account (1). They conduct the course and evaluations, and use the results to draw conclusions for improving the next course and, if applicable, the assessment (2/3). The results and planned changes (4) are communicated to students when possible.

question: How does the University of Bern involve students in QSE?
groundtruth_answer: By participating in surveys, students can communicate their opinions and are thus involved in the design of teaching.
supporting_sentences: By participating in the surveys, students have the opportunity to communicate their opinions about courses and performance assessments and are thus involved in the design of teaching. Participation rights are anchored in the quality standards for institutional accreditation (quality standard 1.3).

question: Who can faculties contact for support with registration and process questions on course evaluations?
groundtruth_answer: They can contact the Course Evaluation Office at lehrevaluation@unibe.ch.
supporting_sentences: If you have questions about conducting course evaluations or interpreting the evaluation results, please feel free to contact the Course Evaluation Office ("VRQ_Lehrevaluation" <lehrevaluation@unibe.ch>).

question: What is the role of the QSE Commission?
groundtruth_answer: It advises the university management in all matters of quality assurance and quality development.
supporting_sentences: The Commission for Quality Assurance and Quality Development (QSE Commission) advises the university management in all matters of quality assurance and quality development.

question: How are faculty action plans linked to the university action plan?
groundtruth_answer: Measures in the University Action Plan that affect all faculties are incorporated into the Action Plans Faculties and adjusted and supplemented for each faculty.
supporting_sentences: The Action Plans Faculties are also linked to the Action Plan University. Measures in the Action Plan University that affect all faculties are incorporated into the Action Plans Faculties and adjusted and supplemented specifically for each faculty.

question: What should happen if a course receives an 'insufficient' evaluation multiple times?
groundtruth_answer: A renewed interim and final evaluation must be conducted the next time, a self-report is prepared, a discussion held, and for a third time, the instructor attends a didactics course or receives individual counseling.
supporting_sentences: Courses (LV) that have been rated as "insufficient" for the first time: a renewed interim and final evaluation during the next implementation.
Courses that have been rated as "insufficient" for the second time:

a. Instructors prepare a short self-report (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e1006/e855118/e855497/e946563/e998762/e1009020/e1009040/Modell_Selbstbericht_April2020_ger.docx), in which they reflect on their own teaching.
b. The Q-responsible organizes a discussion with the instructors and, if applicable, other persons, in order to jointly identify reasons and search for suitable measures.

Courses that have been rated as "insufficient" for the third time: Instructors attend a course on higher education didactics (https://www.gutelehre.unibe.ch/dienstleistungen/hochschuldidaktik_und_lehrentwicklung/) or make use of individual counseling.

question: What official document defines the regularity of course evaluations?
groundtruth_answer: The framework concept for the implementation and use of course evaluations.
supporting_sentences: The framework concept (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e1006/e855118/e855497/e946563/e998762/e1009019/e1009041/Rahmenkonzept_2024_Final_ger.pdf) for the implementation and use of course evaluations provides an overview of the measures for quality assurance and development (QSE) at the level of individual courses. The most important points of the framework concept are described on this page.

question: What is the purpose of the ALL Award?
groundtruth_answer: The University acknowledges and honors the commitment of its instructors to outstanding teaching, promotes appreciation for excellent teaching, and advances the development of good teaching.
supporting_sentences: With this award, the University acknowledges and honors the commitment of its instructors to outstanding teaching.

ALL contributes to improving the quality of teaching, promoting appreciation for excellent teaching, and advancing the development of good teaching at the University of Bern as a whole. In addition, it especially provides early career researchers with the opportunity to also stand out in teaching.

question: Who reviews ALL nominations and gives out the diplomas?
groundtruth_answer: The faculties review nominations, inform the Teaching Evaluation Office, and deliver the diplomas, which are signed by the Dean.
supporting_sentences: The faculties review the nominations and inform the Teaching Evaluation Office of the awarded courses / instructors.

Faculties access the award template via the university’s internal area, complete it with the relevant information, and print the diploma. The diploma is signed by the Dean and given to the respective individuals.

question: How are courses with multiple instructors handled for ALL nominations?
groundtruth_answer: Only instructors registered in KSL as co-instructors and significantly involved in the course can receive an ALL diploma. For courses with multiple instructors, they are listed together on the diploma.
supporting_sentences: Multiple instructors per ALL nomination:

Only instructors can receive an ALL diploma and be listed on it if they were registered in KSL as co-instructors2 for the respective course and were significantly involved in the organization and execution of the course.
Tutors and other assistants who only performed supporting tasks cannot receive an ALL diploma.

For courses assessed as outstanding that had multiple instructors, they are listed together on the ALL diploma (see example on page 3, usually in alphabetical order). Each listed instructor can receive an ALL diploma (several identical diplomas).

question: Are tutors and assistants eligible for the ALL diploma?
groundtruth_answer: No. Tutors and other assistants who only performed supporting tasks cannot receive an ALL diploma.
supporting_sentences: Tutors and other assistants who only performed supporting tasks cannot receive an ALL diploma.

question: Where are the awarded ALL courses and instructors published?
groundtruth_answer: On the website 'https://www.gutelehre.unibe.ch' and by the faculty QSE (WiMaQ) on the faculty QSE website.
supporting_sentences: The awarded courses and the names of the instructors are published by the LVE Office on the website “https://www.gutelehre.unibe.ch” and by the faculty QSE (WiMaQ) on the faculty QSE website.

question: How are course evaluations conducted (paper or online)?
groundtruth_answer: Since the spring semester 2022, all surveys for final, mid-term, and assessment evaluation are conducted online.
supporting_sentences: Since the spring semester 2022, all surveys for final, mid-term, and assessment evaluation are conducted online.

question: What are some benefits of online course evaluation surveys?
groundtruth_answer: Instructors and admin staff save on printing/scanning, results are provided automatically, supports multiple languages and filter questions, allows for reminders, is sustainable and saves 100,000 sheets of paper per semester.
supporting_sentences: The advantages of online surveys are numerous: instructors and admin staff save on printing and scanning; results are provided automatically and immediately after survey closure; online surveys allow for multiple language versions and filter questions; for surveys with personalized TAN links, automatic reminders are possible; and online surveys are sustainable, saving around 100,000 sheets of paper per semester.

question: How can a course or assessment be registered for evaluation?
groundtruth_answer: Registration is completed via KSL – Kernsystem Lehre – usually by a central office; in exceptional cases, instructors may register for voluntary evaluations.
supporting_sentences: Registration is completed via KSL – Kernsystem Lehre – left tab “Dozierende obligatorisch”. Usually, a central office at the faculty or institute is responsible for registering the courses and assessments to be evaluated. In exceptional cases, instructors may handle registration (mainly for voluntary evaluations).

question: Is automation of evaluation registrations in KSL to the new semester implemented?
groundtruth_answer: No, there is no automation, to avoid administrative idle time. At the start of a semester, there should be a deliberate decision to conduct an evaluation.
supporting_sentences: There is no automation, to avoid administrative idle time. At the start of a semester, there should be a deliberate decision to conduct an evaluation, which someone is responsible for.

question: Are students able to view course evaluation results directly?
groundtruth_answer: No, the Course Evaluation Office does not grant students direct access; however, instructors should discuss results and planned improvements with students.
supporting_sentences: The Course Evaluation Office does not grant students access to evaluation results. However, instructors should discuss survey results and any planned improvements with students wherever possible. Faculties may publish aggregate results through their own channels (e.g. websites).

question: Can individual faculties publish evaluation results?
groundtruth_answer: Yes, faculties may publish internal aggregate results through their own channels.
supporting_sentences: However, it is possible individual faculties may publish internal results through their own channels.

question: Who receives detailed survey results?
groundtruth_answer: Detailed results are usually given only to the instructors included in the evaluation; sometimes also to the person responsible for evaluation at the institute.
supporting_sentences: Detailed results are usually only given to the instructors who were included in the evaluation. In some institutes, the report is also sent to the person responsible for the evaluation. At the end of an evaluation period, aggregate results from evaluations across the faculty are sent to the faculty’s quality managers.

question: How can instructors receive help interpreting evaluation results?
groundtruth_answer: The Course Evaluation Office can be involved at any time for help interpreting results.
supporting_sentences: The Course Evaluation Office can be involved at any time for help interpreting results.

question: Are custom questionnaires allowed for course evaluation?
groundtruth_answer: Individual customization of standard questionnaires is not allowed, but optional additional question blocks can be added; faculties may design their own instruments for feedback but not for official replacement of standard final evaluation.
supporting_sentences: Individual customization of the standard questionnaires is not possible. For the final evaluation, optional additional blocks of questions (supplementary modules) are available, which can be added to the core questionnaire as needed. The sample supplementary modules can be found here (https://www.unibe.ch/studium/werkzeuge_und_arbeitshilfen/fuer_lehrende/lehrveranstaltungsevaluation/schlussevaluation/index_ger.html#pane1101959). Moreover, faculties may design their own survey instruments. The Course Evaluation Office can provide feedback on individually designed questionnaires, but implementation and analysis cannot be done centrally. Custom questionnaires cannot replace mandatory final evaluation with the standard questionnaire.

question: How are questions for evaluators with multiple instructors handled?
groundtruth_answer: If instructors teach independently, individual feedback for each is possible; otherwise, a team evaluation gives joint feedback. No more than three instructors should be individually evaluated per course.
supporting_sentences: If they teach independently of each other, individual feedback for each is meaningful. In that case, select the corresponding instructors in KSL, so that a separate survey is created for each. Note that students must complete a separate survey for each individually evaluated instructor – thus, a maximum of three instructors should be evaluated individually per course. If instructors act as a team, you can select the “team evaluation” option for joint feedback on the whole team.

question: What types of links are used in online evaluations?
groundtruth_answer: Surveys may be conducted with personalized or non-personalized links, depending on evaluation type.
supporting_sentences: A distinction is made between surveys with personalized and non-personalized links. Surveys for mid-term and final evaluations are usually conducted with non-personalized links (https://www.unibe.ch/studium/werkzeuge_und_arbeitshilfen/fuer_lehrende/lehrveranstaltungsevaluation/schlussevaluation/index_ger.html#pane1127465) ("Losung"). Surveys for assessment evaluation are always conducted with personalized links (https://www.unibe.ch/studium/werkzeuge_und_arbeitshilfen/fuer_lehrende/lehrveranstaltungsevaluation/evaluation_der_leistungskontrolle/index_ger.html#pane1065968) ("TAN").

question: What must a self-report include for instructors with 'insufficient' results?
groundtruth_answer: It should comment on evaluation results, recognize strengths and weaknesses, identify areas of action, and any need for support or advice.
supporting_sentences: The self-report is intended to help instructors:
Recognize the strengths and weaknesses in their own teaching;
Be able to respond to the course evaluation results;
Identify areas of action that can be modified or have been modified, and explore possible scope for action;
Point out any need for support or advice.

question: What external tool is recommended for peer observation?
groundtruth_answer: Guide for Peer Observation (PDF) and tools from UZH, such as teachingtools.uzh.ch.
supporting_sentences: Peer Observation – Guide (PDF, 184KB) (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e1006/e855118/e855497/e946563/e998762/e1009021/e1721316/KollegialeHospitationUZH_ger.pdf)
Peer Observation – UniZH Website (https://teachingtools.uzh.ch/en/tools/kollegiale-hospitation)

question: What are some survey instruments mentioned for feedback?
groundtruth_answer: Traffic Light Feedback, Flashlight, Target, Posters with Open Questions, Interim Tests, Muddiest Point.
supporting_sentences: Survey Instruments
Traffic Light Feedback
With this survey method, you quickly (in 2–5 minutes) get an overview of the quantitative distribution of opinions, preferences, or the learning status of your students.
Flashlight
The flashlight is a qualitative survey method in which your students provide information about their learning needs, opinions, or preferences regarding your course.
Target
With the target, you can gather student feedback on various aspects of your course and their characteristics.
Posters with Open Questions
This method allows you to specifically collect qualitative feedback on the strengths and weaknesses of a course, as well as suggestions for improvement.
Interim Tests
With the data from interim tests, you can determine to what extent students have already achieved the objectives of your course.
Muddiest Point
This method is about specifically identifying and then addressing open questions that remain for students.

question: What kind of feedback is the 'Blitzlicht' method best suited for?
groundtruth_answer: For quick, formative feedback about student learning progress or development of the course.
supporting_sentences: You present your students with a short, clear question that interests you for the further development of your course, and record it in writing in a way that is clearly visible to all students. The students answer this question briefly and concisely (no more than two or three sentences) in any order. As the instructor, you note the responses on a flipchart or blackboard and summarize them in terms of content. The Blitzlicht method can also be used as a formative assessment method to learn more about your students' learning progress.

question: When do surveys for assessment evaluation open and close, as standard?
groundtruth_answer: Students receive an email at 8:00 p.m. on the day of the assessment; surveys remain open for 24 hours for oral and 4 days for written assessments.
supporting_sentences: Students receive an email with the access link to the questionnaire at 8:00 p.m. on the day of the assessment.

The surveys remain open for 24 hours (oral assessments) or 4 days (written assessments and all other types) and close automatically. For surveys that last 4 days, a reminder is sent after 2 days to students who have not yet completed the survey.
